In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metabolic changes observed in the needles of the ozone-treated spruce trees are a result of a combination of the effects of both the ozone and the soil factors.
ozone and acid mist have no significant influence on the energy status of the needles of the spruce trees.
the soil factor is of great importance for the response of plants to air pollutants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metabolic changes in needles of spruce trees are not only caused by the air pollution, but also by soil factors.
ozone and acid mist are not the only factors which determine the physiological status of the needles.
ozone and acid mist, in combination with soil factors, are able to induce a significant alteration of the carbohydrate and energy status in needles of spruce trees.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metabolic status in needles of spruce trees was not only influenced by ozone and acid rain, but also by the type of soil.
the soil is a factor of importance in determining the effects of air pollutants on plants.
the physiological state of a plant is not only influenced through air pollution.
